The coordinator assigned #7918's identity:

- **ICFG pair:** v110/v109. Master is at v100/v99.
- **Policy token:** `-7918-go-field-selector-addressability`.
- **JVM gate:** the new hook leaves values unchanged by default and adds no JVM reads, so the coordinator may approve it by reviewing the diff instead of running the full JVM gate. I'll send the pushed head and the exact shared changes, and hold #7918 out of ready until the coordinator answers.
- **PR B:** once #7918 lands and PR B merges it, PR B gets a new ICFG pair from the coordinator at that point.

I've recorded all of this. Still waiting on the #7918 fix and the rest of PR B checkpoint 4.

The #7918 fix works: every Go test and the new 12-probe golden pass. But reviewing the shared code turned up two problems that would affect the JVM, so I sent it back before committing:

- **A new read for every language:** the block looks up each field's language by reading from storage, every time a field is projected, in every language. That's new read cost on the JVM path, which would block the diff-review approval the coordinator offered. The language has to come from something already in memory.
- **Duplicated values:** even when the hook leaves a value unchanged, a field with two recorded receivers gets its value added twice. The shared step will now run only for a language that opts in through a flag that defaults to off, which is just Go. Every other language skips it entirely, with the same values in the same order and no new reads.

The only test failure is the known #7506 cold-start count, which happens before this code runs.

Once that's fixed, I'll apply the identity changes (v110/v109 and the token), open the PR, and send the coordinator the exact shared changes.

PR B checkpoint 4 is still working through its remaining items.

The #7918 fix is up as draft PR #7925 (head `02eeb50373`).

- **What it fixes:** Go code can now call a pointer-receiver method through a field reached via a pointer or addressable variable, like `p.inner.PtrMethod()` or `s.mu.Lock()`.
- **JVM side:** I checked the revised shared code myself. The language now comes from what the evaluation already holds, so there are no new reads. Every language except Go skips the new block entirely, and Go's results are de-duplicated.
- **Identity:** ICFG v110/v109 and the token are applied.
- **Tests:** the identity tests pass, as do the Go tests and goldens. The new 12-probe golden covers both allowed and rejected calls.

I sent the reviewer the PR and gave the coordinator the exact shared lines (`language_support.rs:167` and `:174`, `fact_resolution.rs:50924-50935` and `:51107-51143`). That's so the coordinator can decide whether its JVM gate result can stand on a review of the diff. #7925 stays a draft until both answer. When it lands, PR B merges it and gets a new ICFG pair.

PR B checkpoint 4 is still working through its remaining items.

The coordinator approved #7925 (#7918) for the JVM by reviewing the diff, so it doesn't need a full JVM gate run. It confirmed that every non-Go language skips the new code, with no reads and identical values, and that the identity changes are correct. I added that to the PR description.

The coordinator flagged one Go-side effect, not a blocker. Go field values that used to appear twice, once per receiver, now appear once. If a Go golden counts values, that's why.

PR B's next ICFG pair will be v116/v115. I'll apply it only when PR B merges master after #7924 lands, so it changes just once.

PR B checkpoint 4 made progress and raised one design question I've taken to the reviewer.

**Done:**
- Stdlib imports discovered by the Go toolchain now get model types.
- The old `Stop` test is narrowed, after I saw its before and after. Its checks for declared members still pass.
- 3,338 of 3,340 library tests pass, along with 341 of 344 broader tests, Clippy, and the reach-in gate.

I committed the work as a checkpoint marked incomplete, and merged master into it so the agent can use #7872's local-variable lookup for the receiver classification.

**The design question:** routing every Go receiver call through the native path loses answers in three places where today's code gets them by guessing at a model function's result type:
- **Typestate:** a typestate check goes incomplete, because the type of `f, _ := os.Open(...)` comes from a model function's return value. Typing those natively is the later G1b milestone's job.
- **Receiver-storage:** the receiver-storage policy loses a finding, because no model type is recorded for `*http.Request` there.
- **Interface calls:** an interface method call is now named exactly, but the policy query language's rules need a fully proven call target to use it, so they lose precision.

**My proposal to the reviewer:** route natively only where the native engine already knows the receiver's model type, and keep today's path everywhere else until G1b removes it. The plan already keeps that legacy code alive until G1b. This way PR B only adds native answers and doesn't trade lost policy findings for G1b. I'm holding those three areas until the reviewer answers.

Also running: the post-merge tests for #7925 (the #7918 fix). It becomes ready after that.

The reviewer agreed to the narrower PR B routing for two of the three cases, with conditions. They held back on the third. I passed the decisions to the agent:

- **Typestate and receiver-storage:** keep today's answer only when the native result names one of two specific known gaps that the later G1b milestone fills. The first is a receiver type that comes from a model function's return value. The second is a model type behind an import the native engine hasn't indexed. Every other result stays native, because a "native found nothing, so fall back" rule would hide bugs like #7918.
- **Tracking:** each fallback is counted by reason in the differential output, so G1b can show the count reaches zero before deleting both code paths. The PR description will list every site that falls back.
- **The interface-call case:** no preference for the old answer yet. First establish whether the old "fully proven" answer was backed by real data the native engine could read. If so, the native answer is a bug to fix. If not, the native answer is the correction.

Another session (d8443f17) asked how to port its #7351 change now that 3a part 2 rewrote the code it touches. #7351 extends the Go failure-handler policy so it can prove whether a type has an `Error() string` method. My answers:

1. **The method-set walk it used is legacy code #7509 retires**, so it must not add a new caller. The native equivalent is the Go member lookup in the native engine, which already handles embedded fields, pointer versus value receivers, and knowing when a type's method list is complete. PR B extends that lookup to model types and adds a shared entry point for asking about one method on a receiver type. The proof will read: method found with the right signature means an error value; a complete method list without it means not a handler; anything else stays open.
2. **The native declared-type answer is enough to identify the type**, if the port uses the type's identity from the answer rather than its printed name, and checks completeness first. That keeps unresolved, generic and unindexed library types open.
3. **Their lane does the port, with my review.** It builds on PR B's branch once I push it as a draft, because the entry point and model support live there. Meanwhile they can move the parts that don't need the method lookup onto master.

how is go-legacy removal progressing? is there additional work we can do in parallel?

**Progress.** About half of #7509 has landed. What remains is mostly the deeper resolver and model-inference families, which come after PR B.

| Status | Work |
|---|---|
| Landed earlier | Dead-code removal (#7511, #6566), M1 (#7527), M2 (#7791), the shared model seam G1a-i (#7567), promotion-copy marking (#7597) |
| Landed today | 3a part 1 (#7808), the type-switch and variadic producer fix (#7819), G1a-ii PR A (#7811), 3a part 2 (#7872), plus the module-cache bound (#7665) and the plan update (#7900) |
| In the merge queue | #7925, the field-addressability fix (#7918) that PR B depends on |
| In progress | G1a-ii PR B, checkpoint 4 of 4 (routing). Checkpoints 1-3 are committed. The agent is adding the typed fallback and its counter. |
| Not started | The last 3a item, 3b, 3c, G1b, M5 and M6/G2 |

PR B has a new result: today's "fully proven" answer for `fmt.Stringer.String` had no complete list of implementations behind it. So the native "family still open" answer is the correction, and the agent will update that golden with a cause per line rather than keep the old answer.

**Parallel work.** Most of the remaining milestones are blocked by PR B. G1b builds on it, and 3b, the last 3a item and the #7351 port all touch the same Go definition code. A3-Go is already running in 28c4a33b's lane. Four things are not blocked:

1. **M5 census (read-only).** M5 moves import resolution in `go/diagnostics.rs` onto native import facts, migrates two alias checks off the old code, then deletes the import-edge half of the Go workspace index. That index has only two users left (`go/mod.rs` and `bifrost-go/src/graph/resolver.rs`). The map would show which parts avoid PR B's files. The `diagnostics.rs` part probably does; the alias checks partly overlap `get_definition/go.rs`.
2. **M6 design census (read-only).** The plan requires a query and schema proposal for the coordinator before M6, the milestone that deletes the Go workspace graph and cache. Mapping today's hierarchy and member-family readers is pure reading. I'd write the proposal myself.
3. **#7920.** This is the follow-up to #7918 for the second code path that still marks fields addressable unconditionally. It needs #7925's hook, so it can start once #7925 lands, or from its head now.
4. **The declared-type part of #7862.** 28c4a33b took the shortcut for local definitions. The declared-type query's repeated reads are unowned shared engine work.

**Recommendation.** Start items 1 and 2 now as read-only maps; they're cheap and settle the order for after PR B. Start item 3 when #7925 lands. Leave item 4 unless read cost becomes the priority. Say which you want and I'll start them.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- What limits parallel work here is file contention: almost every remaining milestone edits `get_definition/go.rs` or the Go native-points path, the same code PR B is rewriting. That's why the read-only maps are the safe parallel work.
- PR B's fallback to the old code runs only for named reasons (a receiver type that comes from a model function's return, or a model type behind an unindexed import), and each fallback is counted. A bare "native found nothing" rule would have hidden bugs like #7918. The counter lets G1b prove the old code is no longer used before deleting it.
- The fully-proven interface answer was an assumption with no list of implementations behind it, so the native answer is more honest, not a regression. Checking inventory evidence before preferring the old answer is how this effort separates real regressions from corrections.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
